note: v1, THE DRONE (first round; Harry, 12 Nov: "get even a drone in place so we can start the playlist and replace it on round 2"). A placeholder so the groove can open to the song: 48 bars, 1:34, 126 bpm, on the home note F. LISTEN FOR: a bowed low F that never moves, its fifth arriving at 0:15, a ride bell on every quarter-note from 0:15 (the pulse: common time, plainly), and two clean-guitar cells ticking over it - five sixteenths long on the left from 0:08, seven on the right from 0:30 - which drift against the bar and against each other and strike together every 35 sixteenths; one open low string of the 8-string at 0:30 and 1:01. Library patches only; nothing here is the new sound family yet (that is being built and measured against the old one now) and none of it is meant to survive round 2 except the home note, the pulse and the two cells. Measured, not heard: -12.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29, left and right within 1 dB in every 8 bars. compscore 85.9 (length 0 by design: the slot is 12-14 minutes).
next: round 2 replaces the drone: the new guitar, bass and kit family (bench running) and the piece's opening sections

note: v2, THE WHOLE PIECE, ROUGH (whole-song round; Harry, 12 Nov: "get the song down so i can start listening to it and then we can refine a great deal over time"). The drone is replaced by all thirteen minutes: 409 bars at 126 bpm, 13:03. WHAT IT IS: one steady pulse in 4/4 that never breaks, and three WHEELS under it - riff cells five, seven and eleven sixteenths long - that start together at bar 1 and keep turning for the whole piece, heard or not. All three meet the bar line again only at bar 386 (5 x 7 x 11 bars later, 12:13): the piece is that wait, and what it lands on is plain common time, a cell eight sixteenths long with the snare on 2 and 4, for the first and only time. On the way two wheels at a time meet on a bar line, and those meetings are the section boundaries (so the form, 35 20 15 7 28 5 30 14 11 10 / 35 / 10 11 14 30 5 28 7 15 20 35 bars, is a palindrome nobody chose); the two that have just met are what the next section is made of. LISTEN FOR: 0:00 one strike of everything, then only clean ticks (five on the left, seven on the right from 0:23, eleven in the middle from 0:42); 1:06 riff A, the five wheel, full band; 1:44 eleven's open chords ringing over it; 2:13 seven bars of the seven wheel nearly alone; 2:26 riff B (seven) with the bass on eleven, and the lead's tune from 2:53 (one note to each turn of the eleven wheel); 3:20 stop-time, sixteen stabs; 3:29 riff C, the eleven wheel, the same shape pulled apart, slow and wide; 4:26 five in the left guitar against seven in the right; 4:53 the lead runs; 5:33 the eye: the ticks alone again, the tune an octave down; 6:40 the weight returns and the sections come back in mirror order, heavier (8:53 the hardest stretch: sixteenth-note kick, a semitone up and back at 9:20); 11:06 the approach, all three wheels at once; 12:13 THE LANDING; 12:43 the last chord rings out over the ticks. A crash marks every bar line where a sounding wheel starts a turn. THE SOUND: the rhythm guitars are the first of the new family, ct-chug-l / ct-chug-r (patches/, sounds.md): the old m8-obzen pair with the engine's white-box amp (triode preamp stages, a push-pull power amp inside a feedback loop driving a speaker), a longer pitch settle on the slack low string, more scrape and sympathetic ring. Measured against two records' guitar stems (tools/riffpunch.py, old pair -> new): Bleed 41.4 -> 67.0, The Faultless 37.8 -> 69.1 (the separators' floor is 67-86); 30 candidates, in ~/.local/state/chirper-zero/c10. A/B on riff A, old rig then new, same notes: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-rig-old-new-ab.mp3 (full band) and http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-rig-old-new-guitars-only-ab.mp3. Bass, kit, clean guitar and lead are still the old family (bass-fat, obzen-kit-dry, m8-clean, m8-lead-guitar): next. WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): every section's level and left/right (heavy sections -13.3 to -14.6 dBFS rms, the opening -20.9, the eye -20.1; left and right within 0.5 dB except the 7-bar seven break, +1.6 left by design: the right guitar enters four bars late); each track against the mix in three windows (tools/presence.py): the first draft had the cymbals LOUDEST everywhere (2 dB under the mix; now 8.6) and the bass 17 dB under (now 9.4); band shares of the heavy sections against seven records of the genre: inside their range in every band (90-355 Hz 2 dB under their median). -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29, no flat-topping. KNOWN ROUGH: the lead in the eye is 9 dB over the ticks (too far forward); the kick is the loudest thing in riff A; the sections differ in which wheels play but not yet enough in style; every fill is the same run; no vocals; nothing has been heard by anyone. compscore 94.46 (the v1 drone 85.9): structure, variety, rhythm, master, length 100; recurrence 68.8 (17 of 21 sections return: too alike). motifs.md, styles.md, sounds.md.
next: the kit and the bass (new family, measured), then the sections' styles: make the mirror half differ from the first, the eye's balance, real fills, the lead's sound
